competitive_landscape: The water is run today by traditional diesel water taxis (penambang) serving Kampong Ayer and a sheltered-bay passenger ferry chain linking the capital to Labuan and Kota Kinabalu, plus the oil sector's substantial crew-transfer fleet. The penambang prove a deep, durable daily water-commuting habit; the cross-bay ferries and offshore fleet are diesel and ageing. The demand to move by water is already embedded — the opportunity is to make it clean, quiet and fast.

journeys.today: Diesel water taxis (penambang) buzz across the river constantly — cheap and frequent, but noisy, fume-emitting and wake-heavy past a heritage settlement.
journeys.with_navier: A clean, quiet foiling tier on the same crossing the village already commutes by — modernising a centuries-old water habit with zero local emissions.

journeys.today: A ~45-minute slow boat shuttle across Brunei Bay, or a long drive over the 2020 bridge.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth ~25 nm all-electric foiling passage across the sheltered bay to the rainforest gateway, quiet and wake-light into the eco-lodge jetties.

journeys.today: A long road drive around the Limbang corridor with border crossings, or no direct sea link.
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~25 nm cross-border foiling run over coastal water — a fast, smooth business link between the two Borneo cities.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The capital's working network is all in all-electric range: the Kampong Ayer river commute and Brunei Bay hops (5–15 nm), the Temburong gateway (~25 nm), and the short cross-border legs to Miri (~25 nm) and Labuan (~30 nm). Sheltered bay water and an abundant, high-quality urban grid make this a clean all-electric environment for both daily commuting and premium transfers.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The longer cross-bay reach to Kota Kinabalu (~130 nm) and offshore oil-platform crew transfers exceed all-electric range and suit the long-range hybrid — which refuels on the country's abundant, low-cost domestic diesel and needs no new charging infrastructure, a natural fit for an energy-rich market.

precedents.what: ~100-vessel, $100M phased clean-marine network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows a clean-marine network financed and operated at scale in a compact, water-defined state — a credible model for a small, energy-rich maritime nation building a premium clean-mobility tier.

regulatory_note: Certification and port operations run through the national maritime and port authority under the transport ministry, a small-country single-window pathway comparable to other compact maritime states — structurally fast for first-of-class approval. An abundant, subsidised domestic fuel supply makes long-range-hybrid refuelling trivial, and a high-quality urban grid supports all-electric charging at the capital. Cross-border legs to Miri and Labuan require Malaysia–Brunei immigration coordination at designated terminals.
seasonality: Brunei sits south of the Philippine typhoon belt, with parallel southwest (May–Sep) and northeast (Nov–Mar) monsoons that lift some swell on the open South China Sea coast but leave the Brunei River and Brunei Bay largely sheltered year-round. Foiling smooths the short coastal chop on the cross-border legs; the core river and bay network is calm-water for most of the year.

summary: Bandar Seri Begawan is one of the few capitals where the water is already the street. Kampong Ayer, the world's largest stilt settlement, is home to tens of thousands of residents who move by water taxi every day — a deep, living water-commuting habit to modernise rather than create. Beyond the river, sheltered Brunei Bay links the capital to Temburong's rainforest, and short sea legs reach across the border to Sarawak and Labuan. In an oil-wealthy market with a premium appetite and abundant fuel, clean, fast, near-silent foiling fits both the daily commute and the cross-bay reach.
tagline: A capital built on the water — the world's largest stilt village already commutes by boat; now make it fly.

use_cases.body: Bring a clean, near-silent foiling tier to the river commute that the water village already runs by boat every day — quieter, wake-light and zero-emission for daily movement between Kampong Ayer, the capital waterfront and Muara.
use_cases.title: Modernise the Kampong Ayer commute

use_cases.body: Short all-electric cross-border legs to Miri and Labuan for business travel, with a long-range hybrid reaching Kota Kinabalu and offshore oil-platform crew transfers — refuelling on abundant local diesel, no charging infrastructure required.
